question: The conductivity of a semiconductor increases when its temperature is increased, while that of a metal decreases. Explain this difference with reason.

options.A: Heating decreases carrier concentration in semiconductors but increases free-electron concentration in metals, so metal conductivity increases.
options.B: Heating affects neither semiconductors nor metals because charge carriers and mobility never change.
options.C: In a semiconductor, heating creates more electron-hole pairs across the small band gap, increasing carrier concentration and conductivity. In a metal, heating increases lattice vibrations and electron collisions, reducing electron mobility and hence decreasing conductivity.
options.D: Both semiconductors and metals become more conductive on heating because lattice vibrations reduce collisions.
